_about: Loanwords that the official vocabularies mark as foreign and that the 1911 digraph and geminate rules would still rewrite (apartheid -> aparteid, hall -> hal, byte -> bite). The 1911 Formulário, Base I, covers "todas as palavras portuguesas, ou aportuguesadas", so a listed foreign word keeps its spelling under 1911-digraphs and 1911-geminates. The table is closed: a form is here only when the VOP marks its lemma "estrangeirismo" or the VOLP marks it "Estrangeira" (Vocabulário de Estrangeirismos), and the rules change it. A spelling mark and the attested-word check both fail on these words: byte gives bite, which the VOLP lists as a Portuguese word and the VOP lists as a form of bitar. A foreign word that the modern word list holds (cheddar, intelligentsia) stays as written already.
_sources: ABL, Vocabulário Ortográfico da Língua Portuguesa, Vocabulário de Estrangeirismos: https://www.academia.org.br/nossa-lingua/busca-no-vocabulario
Portal da Língua Portuguesa, Vocabulário Ortográfico do Português: https://www.portaldalinguaportuguesa.org/
